newsitem.title: UK: IEA sees less demand for OPEC oil, healthier stock.
newsitem.headline: IEA sees less demand for OPEC oil, healthier stock.

text.p: World oil demand will rise faster than expected in the second and third quarters of this year but strong growth in non-OPEC supply will squeeze further the cartel's market share, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.

The Paris-based agency left unchanged its forecast of world oil demand for the year at 73.7 million barrels per day (bpd), up 1.8 million bpd on 1996, but revised up its forecasts for the second and third quarters by 100,000 bpd to 71.8 million and 72.7 million bpd respectively.

Forecast demand for oil from the 11 members of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) has been revised down by 300,000 bpd to 25.8 million bpd in the fourth quarter and by 100,000 bpd to 25.3 million bpd for the year as a whole.

The lower call on OPEC for 1997 is a result of anticipated strong growth in non-OPEC supply, which rose by 400,000 bpd to 44.91 million bpd in March, the OECD's energy watchdog said in its latest monthly oil market report.
Industry stocks held in OECD countries were drawn down by only 100,000 bpd in the first quarter of the year, compared to a draw of 1.5 million bpd in the same period last year, the IEA said.
